sources.RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria: docs/rfcs/2026-08-21-otp-external-devices.md, task OTP-23 acceptance criteria and verification evidence
sources.user directive 2026-10-26: revision request recorded in docs/otp-23-contract-alignment.md (strict background, attribute budget, macOS identity, plain runtime)
sources.user steering 2026-10-26: account waiver: tests requiring new accounts are non-blocking for OTP-23; recorded as an acceptance scope revision in the RFC
sources.user steering 2026-10-26 (permissions): the user cannot approve Bluetooth permissions now; every phone-, TCC- and background-dependent row stays BLOCKED

rows.requirement: Stable Chrome launches the plain host on demand from a STANDARD non-admin Windows account (new-account test)
rows.expected: Host starts via runtime.connectNative with no elevation; account token is not an administrator. (Historical runs used an administrator account at medium integrity.)
rows.waiver: User-approved acceptance scope revision (2026-10-26): tests requiring NEW accounts are skipped and non-blocking for OTP-23. Not PASS; no fresh or standard-account evidence is claimed.

rows.requirement: Existing-account on-demand launch: stable Chrome starts the plain host via runtime.connectNative and hello -> ready succeeds (non-waived; the standard-account case W-01 stays waived)
rows.expected: Chrome launches the plain host on demand; ready negotiated; account class recorded truthfully. Narrow scope: no phone, no transfer, no link-active cleanup.
rows.actual: CH-02 PASS (reran on the clean cd971f0 native host sha256 6cf72ed0...): launched on demand by runtime.connectNative, hello -> ready; Chrome and wrapper at medium integrity, token not elevated (existing ADMINISTRATOR account's filtered token, not a standard account). Earlier 4e9c685 run also PASS. Proves nothing about phones, transfer or link cleanup.

rows.requirement: Host creates no window and communicates only through Chrome-owned stdin/stdout
rows.expected: Zero top-level windows and zero network endpoints owned by the host and its wrapper during connect, transfer and shutdown.
rows.actual: Clean cd971f0 host, scan/lifecycle cases (and the mixed diagnostic): host_top_level_windows_visible=0, no hidden host windows, no host children, 0 TCP/UDP endpoints. The Chrome-created cmd wrapper had 0 visible windows and 1 HIDDEN window; no claim that the wrapper has no hidden windows. The isolated single-phone run exercised connect and transfer, but without a window-count measurement, so connect/transfer-phase window absence is unproven.
rows.blocker: no window/endpoint measurement during connect and transfer phases; scan-only measurements only

rows.requirement: Extension-owned search receives bounded device events (narrow: one advertising phone)
rows.expected: start_scan yields device_found events within the documented bounds; stop_scan ends them.
rows.actual: Mixed diagnostic windows-single-phone.json CH-05 PASS: scan started, ONE Veles device event within its 4-second observation, scan stopped (correlated request ids); isolated discovery also found one device within 1.5 seconds and stopped its scan. Observed counts are below the documented ceilings of 64 events/second and 1024/scan; upper-rate saturation is software-tested, not physically stress-tested here. Existing administrator account, medium token. Narrow scope: one device; says nothing about two phones.

rows.requirement: Two phones independently exchange synthetic complete records (fresh build of this branch)
rows.expected: Byte-exact replies per original handle for both phones; distinct handles; MTU before CCCD.
rows.actual: SUPPORTING single-phone evidence only (never two-phone): on a clean cd971f0 host, isolated ONE host / ONE scan / ONE phone (OnePlus 6T), byte-exact replies at 4, 508, 509, 1016, 1017, 4095 and 4096 bytes at measured ATT MTU 517, 7 sends and 7 replies in the native trace, explicit disconnect and shutdown, no surviving host (windows/isolated-plain-single-phone.json). The earlier mixed Chrome+phone diagnostic failed PH-01 (no phone in a later 30 s scan); that failure is retained and its cause is UNPROVEN (the isolated run did not reproduce it; multi-host scan interference is consistent but not established). Latest healthy-path refresh on committed e19c8ca: the clean e19c8ca debug APK 1e0ae023... (installed -r, no -g, readback matches both phones) was driven by the unchanged one-host Windows diagnostic (native host 6cf72ed0..., unchanged component): 4, 508, 509, 1016, 1017, 4095, 4096 bytes byte-exact at MTU 517 on the 6T, own host gone, registration/task removed. SUPPORTING single-phone evidence only; no malformed-overload injection, not two-phone/survivor/M6/background.
rows.blocker: two-phone concurrent exchange not run: the OnePlus 10 Pro fixture still lacks Nearby Devices permission (PermissionRequired) and the user cannot approve it now

SUPPORTING single-phone evidence only; no malformed-overload injection, not two-phone/survivor/M6/background.

rows.requirement: Disconnect affects only its handle
rows.expected: Stale handle rejects sends; the surviving phone still exchanges a 4096-byte record.
rows.actual: SUPPORTING single-phone evidence only (never two-phone): on a clean cd971f0 host, isolated ONE host / ONE scan / ONE phone (OnePlus 6T), byte-exact replies at 4, 508, 509, 1016, 1017, 4095 and 4096 bytes at measured ATT MTU 517, 7 sends and 7 replies in the native trace, explicit disconnect and shutdown, no surviving host (windows/isolated-plain-single-phone.json). SUPPORTING single-phone evidence only; no malformed-overload injection, not two-phone/survivor/M6/background.

rows.requirement: Chrome port closure stops scans, disconnects links, closes stdout and leaves no process
rows.expected: Host and wrapper gone after port.disconnect(); BLE links released.
rows.actual: CH-09 and CH-10 (port closure / connector tab close with an ACTIVE SCAN): host exited in about 0.6 s. No BLE link existed, so link release is unproven.
rows.blocker: link-active cleanup not exercised: Both disposable fixtures failed the Nearby Devices prerequisite (PermissionRequired) before advertising; adb grant rejected (GRANT_RUNTIME_PERMISSIONS); the user cannot approve Bluetooth permissions now. No phone was advertising, so no transfer ran.

rows.requirement: stdin EOF stops scans, disconnects links, closes stdout and leaves no process
rows.expected: Same cleanup after the extension stdin pipe closes without a shutdown request.
rows.actual: Scan-only: CH-09 stdin-EOF-equivalent port closure removed the host; no real link existed and a distinct stdin-EOF-without-shutdown case with links was not run.
rows.blocker: link-active cleanup not exercised: Both disposable fixtures failed the Nearby Devices prerequisite (PermissionRequired) before advertising; adb grant rejected (GRANT_RUNTIME_PERMISSIONS); the user cannot approve Bluetooth permissions now. No phone was advertising, so no transfer ran.

rows.requirement: shutdown stops scans, disconnects links, closes stdout and leaves no process
rows.expected: shutdown_complete is the last message; host gone.
rows.actual: CH-08: shutdown with an active scan emitted scan_state stopped then shutdown_complete last and the process exited in 0.69 s. No link existed, so link teardown is unproven.
rows.blocker: link-active shutdown not exercised: Both disposable fixtures failed the Nearby Devices prerequisite (PermissionRequired) before advertising; adb grant rejected (GRANT_RUNTIME_PERMISSIONS); the user cannot approve Bluetooth permissions now. No phone was advertising, so no transfer ran.

rows.requirement: Unsupported or denied radio/permission states are classified
rows.expected: Bluetooth off, adapter absent and access-denied each return a classified error with the documented recoverability.
rows.actual: CH-07: connect to an absent device returned classified connect_failed/device_lookup (retryable); CH-11 reported a missing registration. Bluetooth-off, adapter-absent and access-denied states were not run on Windows.
rows.blocker: radio-off/adapter-absent/denied states not run

rows.requirement: Strict background delivery, COLD idle (no prior exchange)
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: Connector hidden >= 10 min with another ordinary tab focused, NO DevTools client of any kind, no audio/WebRTC/keepalive; both phones' unsolicited 4096-byte records arrive byte-exact while hidden (scripts/strict_background.py --scenario cold).
rows.actual: No strict cold-idle background measurement was run. The 6T later advertised and passed the isolated foreground single-phone exchanges; those are not background or two-phone acceptance evidence.
rows.blocker: The 10 Pro's Nearby Devices permissions remain denied and the user cannot approve them now. Two-phone unsolicited cold-idle delivery and the required continuity/exemption evidence remain unmeasured; historical browser-attached PoC results do not substitute.

rows.requirement: Strict background delivery, PREWARMED link (separate run)
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: Same as W-11 after one byte-verified exchange per phone (--scenario prewarm). Reported separately; never combined with W-11.
rows.actual: No strict prewarmed background measurement was run. The 6T later advertised and passed the isolated foreground single-phone exchanges; those are not background or two-phone acceptance evidence.
rows.blocker: The 10 Pro's Nearby Devices permissions remain denied and the user cannot approve them now. Two-phone unsolicited prewarmed delivery and the required continuity/exemption evidence remain unmeasured; the cold-idle case remains separate.

rows.requirement: Unsigned development-registered host launches from Chrome in a FRESH STANDARD non-admin macOS account (new-account test)
rows.expected: Chrome starts the host; no administrator involvement; a disposable Chrome profile with its own Native Messaging manifest.
rows.waiver: User-approved acceptance scope revision (2026-10-26): tests requiring NEW accounts are skipped and non-blocking for OTP-23. Not PASS; no fresh or standard-account evidence is claimed.

rows.requirement: TCC Bluetooth prompt owner (Chrome vs host) in a FRESH account (new-account test)
rows.expected: Records which process the prompt/grant attaches to and whether a prompt fires for the headless child. (Historical: grant owner unknown; not formal attribution.)
rows.waiver: User-approved acceptance scope revision (2026-10-26): tests requiring NEW accounts are skipped and non-blocking for OTP-23. Not PASS; no fresh or standard-account evidence is claimed.

rows.requirement: Signed production-shaped host (stable bundle identity, usage descriptions, final identifier me.nagaev.veles.bridge) with signing provenance
rows.expected: Directly signed fixture with the final bundle identifier and recorded signing provenance; prompt owner observed on the existing account. NOT waived. (Historical Apple Development me.nagaev.veles.otp23.poc is not proof of the production identity.)
rows.actual: Fresh Aqua packaging of the final identifier me.nagaev.veles.bridge on clean cd971f0: codesign --verify --strict AND the cryptographic -R='anchor apple generic' check PASSED in the actual packaging command; Apple Development stable identity; unsigned raw host sha256 c36894dc...64ea, signed host sha256 e7c716c5...eb91c. This is Apple Development, NOT Developer ID, notarized or CI-provided signing provenance. (Earlier 4e9c685 fixture hashes are history.)
rows.blocker: no Developer ID / CI signing provenance, no notarization; prompt owner not observed

rows.requirement: DENY result and exact System Settings retry guidance
rows.expected: Deny produces access_denied with exact System Settings guidance; the prompt owner (Chrome vs host) is recorded as observed on the existing account; no TCC reset used.
rows.actual: Clean cd971f0 signed final-identifier fixture: headless Chrome launch, hello -> ready, then scan stage access_denied with CoreBluetooth authorization denied (existing TCC state; no prompt shown to a human; prompt owner NOT observed). No deny walk-through, allow or recovery. No TCC reset or bypass was used.
rows.blocker: requires a human on the existing account to drive the prompt; the user cannot approve Bluetooth permissions now

rows.requirement: ALLOW result
rows.expected: Allow yields allowed_always and discovery works for the same binary.
rows.blocker: requires a human to allow Bluetooth for the final-identifier fixture on the existing account; the user cannot approve it now (account class: existing administrator, recorded truthfully)

rows.requirement: Recovery after deny -> allowed_always with the SAME extension state, no reinstall
rows.expected: After granting in System Settings, search recovers without reinstalling and without losing extension state.
rows.blocker: requires a human grant and the same extension state across denied -> allowed_always; not possible now; no recovery claimed

rows.requirement: Two phones independently exchange synthetic complete records incl. attribute-budget boundaries (fresh build)
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria + user directive 2026-10-26
rows.expected: Byte-exact for the W-05 size list on both phones using the measured max write-without-response (512 -> attribute 512, payload 508; no invented MTU).
rows.actual: No fresh macOS transfer or background measurement: CoreBluetooth authorization is denied for the signed final-identifier fixture and the user cannot approve it now; no phone fixture advertised.
rows.blocker: CoreBluetooth denied (human grant unavailable) and phone fixture permissions unavailable

rows.requirement: No window; port closure, stdin EOF and shutdown each leave no process
rows.expected: As W-02, W-07, W-08, W-09 on macOS.
rows.actual: Clean cd971f0 signed fixture: Chrome launched the host on demand, ready negotiated, no on-screen host window observed (trace), scan failed access_denied. Port-closure, EOF and shutdown cleanup with links were not run.

rows.requirement: Interop defects found by the physical runs are fixed or recorded (#120 M3 duplicate STATE_CONNECTED, M4 CCCD/MTU ordering)
rows.expected: Duplicate connected callback keeps a healthy link; MTU-before-CCCD observed on Windows and macOS clients; CCCD-before-MTU rejected with record I/O gated.
rows.actual: Windows MTU-before-CCCD observed again in the isolated single-phone host trace (mtu=517 line precedes 'subscribed'); duplicate-callback behavior has JVM tests only. macOS was not observed because CoreBluetooth is denied. #120 M3/M4 physical confirmation therefore remains incomplete.
rows.blocker: macOS ordering unobserved (CoreBluetooth denied) and the duplicate STATE_CONNECTED case has no physical observation

rows.requirement: #120 M6: two CENTRALS on ONE phone (independent 4096-byte downstream records, no cross-peer disconnect)
rows.expected: Explicitly different from two phones on one central; not discharged by W-04/M-07.
rows.blocker: M6 needs two centrals on ONE phone and a second central; only a single Windows central ran. The 6T alone is usable, but no second central or concurrent-central procedure was run; two phones on one central never discharge M6

rows.requirement: Current Tauri-vs-plain cost evaluation and an explicit retention decision for Tauri used solely for OTP-25 packaging
rows.expected: A recorded current comparison (sizes, build, dependency graphs, SBOMs) and an explicit decision. Evaluation only: no bundler/installer is implemented or required in OTP-23. A negative decision is a valid outcome (the RFC allows OTP-25 another pipeline).
rows.actual: Current native plain vs dependency-linked Tauri (event loop not started), snapshot 4e9c685: Windows 717,312 vs 758,272 B, 22 vs 276 SBOM components; macOS 1,721,088 vs 1,744,368 B, 46 vs 275 (macOS-target SBOMs generated on Linux with cargo-cyclonedx 0.5.9; macOS builds native). Windows cost binaries differ from the Chrome-installed hash; no reproducibility claim. DECISION: retaining Tauri solely for packaging is NOT APPROVED and NOT JUSTIFIED by this cost proxy (+254 components on Windows, +229 on macOS). OTP-25 must choose another packaging pipeline, or provide a separately reviewed justification (including a bundler proof) to revisit retention. This PASS records completion of the evaluation and the negative decision; it is not approval of Tauri, packaging readiness or OTP-24 GO.

rows.requirement: Explicit OTP-23 feasibility decision recorded from the per-row dispositions
rows.expected: A recorded decision. GO requires every row PASS except NOT RUN rows carrying the user-approved account waiver; otherwise NO-GO for OTP-24. PASS here means the decision was recorded, not that OTP-24 is eligible.
rows.actual: Decision recorded: NO-GO for OTP-24. Eligibility for GO is NOT met: the matrix still has blocking rows (two-phone and failure-isolation, link-active cleanup, M6, strict background cold/prewarm, macOS permission/signing/allow/deny/recovery, unsigned-host M-11, the 10 Pro permission prerequisite, and the other BLOCKED rows). Only W-01, M-01, M-02 are non-blocking account-waived NOT RUN. This PASS does not claim OTP-23 satisfied, approve OTP-24 or close any issue.

rows.requirement: Unsigned dev-registered host on the EXISTING account: launch, TCC authorization and scan, compared with the signed fixture (original RFC unsigned-versus-signed requirement; only the fresh-account part is waived)
rows.expected: The unsigned dev-registered binary is launched by Chrome from a disposable profile; its TCC authorization and scan result are recorded and compared with M-03..M-06; account class recorded truthfully (admin or standard).
rows.blocker: not executed: the unsigned dev-registered host's CoreBluetooth authorization on the existing account cannot be granted now (the user cannot approve Bluetooth permissions) and no unsigned-host run was made; no result exists

rows.requirement: Nearby Devices permission granted to the disposable `.otp23` fixture on each phone (prerequisite for every phone row)
rows.expected: Instrumentation prerequisite passes (SharingState.prerequisite null) and the fixture advertises on both phones.
rows.actual: Nearby Devices state is per phone. OnePlus 6T: BLUETOOTH_CONNECT and ADVERTISE GRANTED at observation (grant mechanism NOT observed); its first 10 s bounded attempt was stopped before a result (not a pass and not a PermissionRequired failure), then a fresh fixture held and reached otp23-ready and ended OK (1 test). OnePlus 10 Pro: both DENIED; the fixture fails PermissionRequired. Clean cd971f0 debug APK 6382bf28... installed as an update on both (readback hashes match; no -g, no app-data clearing). Earlier dirty-fb224e8 APK 469826666... and the first failures are retained, not relabelled. Latest: clean e19c8ca APK 1e0ae023... installed as an update on both phones (readback matches; no -g, no data clearing); the 6T fixture held and ended OK (1 test); the 10 Pro remains Nearby-Devices denied. Single-phone only.
rows.blocker: the OnePlus 10 Pro still denies Nearby Devices and the user cannot approve it now; only the 6T fixture can run (single phone), so every two-phone criterion stays blocked

rows.requirement: Required local gates on the normal build (spotlessCheck detekt lintDebug testDebugUnitTest protocolCheck) and both raw android.util.Log guards
rows.source: RFC OTP-23 acceptance criteria / repository rules
rows.expected: All succeed on the integrated tree (re-run after every code fix).
rows.actual: COMMITTED e19c8ca555b3275313cd325a12e15791a2cf894d, clean rebuild after the commit: same-shell log linux-clean-gates.log (exported JAVA_HOME=/home/dev/.jdk/zulu21, Gradle launcher Azul 21.0.12.1, daemon /home/dev/.jdk/zulu21) with spotlessCheck detekt lintDebug testDebugUnitTest protocolCheck and assembleRelease, exit 0; 321 JVM tests, 0 failures/errors/skipped (SharingGattServerTest 22, from the JUnit XML). The ci.yml guard body (ci-log-guards.sh, source-equal) ran under bash -v with both greps shown, no matches, guard_exit_code 0 (ci-log-guards-verbatim.log). Clean release APK 810aef8d... (unsigned) re-inspected: all DEX + R8 mapping lack SyntheticTransportFixture/scheduleSyntheticPush/OTP23_POC; no scan/location permission; not debuggable. Debug APK 1e0ae023... version 0.0.3-29-e19c8ca-contract_otp23-desktop-alignment (no dirty suffix). Restoring the silent postValue drop fails 3 non-control tests (mutation-silent-postvalue.log). HISTORY, each keeping its own source identity: ingress-final/ (321 tests on the same code before the commit), cd971f0 (316 tests, APK 6382bf28..., release a424caf7...), 4e9c685 and older; post-review/log-guards.log and jdk.txt remain non-proof.

rows.requirement: Native Rust build, test and clippy -D warnings executed on the real Windows and macOS targets (current clean source)
rows.expected: cargo test --locked, cargo clippy --locked --all-targets -- -D warnings and cargo build --release --locked --bin otp23-host exit 0 on x86_64-pc-windows-msvc and aarch64-apple-darwin (Rust 1.98.0) from the clean submitted source.
rows.actual: Clean committed cd971f0, verified source archive sha256 e34d279b...c667cb on both desktops: all three commands exit 0. Windows host sha256 6cf72ed0...fcda (717,312 B); macOS 165 tests, clippy and release build pass, raw host sha256 c36894dc...64ea. Ignored radio tests are not passes. No reproducibility claim. The earlier 4e9c685 results (host hashes 09713016..., 6ba7fad8...) are history, not current.
